milestone: Pure scalar GPU choices and strict float32 comparisons
implementation: All six float32 comparisons lower to integer operations over bit encodings, matching CPU ordered comparison semantics without native float comparisons

Pure scalar conditional arms support float32/internal Boolean results, local bindings, nesting and Boolean logic; cached bounded purity analysis rejects tensor work, primitives, shape checks and effects inside arms
Selections copy float32 bits using integer select and bitcasts; no unqualified native floating selection or branch-dependent allocation/dispatch
Reduction dependency analysis retains values used by predicates as well as selected arms; choices compose with tensor feedback and multiple-reduction scalar joins

Conditional graphs use the existing Tier 2 force-active-resource interface even for small signatures; graph preflight accepts those validated signatures, preserving bindings when optimization removes a predicate or an identical arm
Function signatures and public scalar captures retain the existing float32 boundary; Boolean helper signatures/captures and tensor-valued branches remain unsupported

qualification.reference: LLVM APFloat comparison predicates and division; encoded truth-table results compare exactly, numerical NaNs compare by classification
cases: All six predicates over the cross-product of 16 IEEE edge encodings plus 128 random/neighbor pairs: signed zeros, positive/negative subnormals, normal boundaries, finite extrema, infinities and quiet/signaling NaNs
Each pair checks both a six-predicate truth-table encoding and conditional normalization using a resident one-element reduction
Boolean and/not logic, or expressions inside float32 helpers, nested scalar choices, branch-local bindings and signed-zero selection
Reductions used only by a predicate, constant predicates, identical arms in a tensor map, multiple-reduction final joins and identical arms in scalar joins
Thirty-three allocation failure checkpoints and cancellation/deadline/device failure at both commands preserve owned-capture and buffer accounting
Conditional tensor computations and reductions in arms retain transactional rejection; unused numerical primitives remain diagnostics
Ten CLI scenarios including relocated output, each run with 1/2/4 workers in all four modes
Installed Release compiler builds scalar-control graphs; relocated applications continue working after compiler resources are removed

remaining: Tensor-stage control flow and fallible/effectful branch arms
Wider GPU numeric types, broader ranks, Boolean helper signatures/captures and Boolean storage interfaces
Optimization: derive projected direct bindings from the lowered interface while preserving constant/identical-arm behavior
